Plot correlations within two strata as split triangles

Source: R/PlotSplitCorrelationHeatmap.R
PlotSplitCorrelationHeatmap.Rd

Each cell represents the same predictor-outcome pair in two strata of long data. The first selected stratum occupies the top-left triangle and the second occupies the bottom-right triangle. Correlations are calculated by PlotCorrelationsHeatmap() independently within each stratum, including covariate adjustment and FDR correction.

Usage

PlotSplitCorrelationHeatmap(
  data,
  predictor_vars = NULL,
  outcome_vars = NULL,
  split_var,
  split_levels = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  method = "pearson",
  Relabel = TRUE,
  TreatOrdinalAs = "Categorical",
  min_n = 3,
  eps = 1e-12,
  fdr_scope = c("matrix", "per_outcome", "per_predictor"),
  IncludeTrendSymbol = FALSE,
  interactive = c("none", "plotly")
)

Arguments

data

A long data frame with one column per measured variable and a column identifying the stratum of each record.

predictor_vars, outcome_vars

Character vectors passed to PlotCorrelationsHeatmap(). Predictors are rows and outcomes are columns. Defaults use numeric predictors (excluding split_var) and the same variables as outcomes.

split_var

Name of the column identifying strata.

split_levels

Two observed values of split_var, in triangle order. If omitted, exactly two observed values are required; factor order is respected, otherwise first-observed order is used.

covariates, method, Relabel, TreatOrdinalAs, min_n, eps, fdr_scope, IncludeTrendSymbol

Passed to PlotCorrelationsHeatmap(). FDR correction is performed separately within each stratum, before any display alignment.

interactive

Either "none" (default) or "plotly". Static plots are always returned; Plotly widgets require the suggested plotly package.

Value

A list with Unadjusted and FDRCorrected, each containing a static plot and named lists of matrices r, p, and npairs, indexed by split level. p and p_fdr alias these branches. Correlations holds the source results; Results contains one row per stratum and cell; Metadata records settings, axis order, counts, and unavailable results. Optional widgets are in Interactive$Plotly$Unadjusted and Interactive$Plotly$FDRCorrected.

Details

Stars test the correlation within each stratum, not the difference between strata. This function performs no between-stratum comparison test. Missing split values are excluded with a warning. Unavailable correlations remain visible as gray triangles, with counts and status in Results. Unadjusted refers to raw p-values; requested covariate adjustment is retained in both output branches.

Labels are inherited from the source correlation results (normally attached from a codebook using RevalueData()). Variable identifiers, rather than labels, determine cell identity, so duplicate display labels are supported.

Author

Aparna Bhattacharyya (original split-triangle wrapper).

Examples

set.seed(42)
df_Example <- data.frame(
  Compartment = factor(rep(c("Plasma", "CSF"), each = 30)),
  IL6 = rnorm(60), TNF = rnorm(60), Cognition = rnorm(60),
  Age = runif(60, 25, 75)
)
df_Example$IL6 <- sjlabelled::set_label(df_Example$IL6, "Interleukin-6")
df_Example$TNF <- sjlabelled::set_label(df_Example$TNF, "Tumor necrosis factor")
df_Example$Cognition <- sjlabelled::set_label(
  df_Example$Cognition, "Cognitive score"
)
result <- PlotSplitCorrelationHeatmap(
  df_Example, predictor_vars = c("IL6", "TNF"),
  outcome_vars = "Cognition", split_var = "Compartment",
  split_levels = c("Plasma", "CSF"), covariates = "Age"
)
result$FDRCorrected$plot

# Optional interactive version:
# result <- PlotSplitCorrelationHeatmap(
#   df_Example, c("IL6", "TNF"), "Cognition", "Compartment",
#   covariates = "Age", interactive = "plotly"
# )
# result$Interactive$Plotly$FDRCorrected
